resources.string: What it can and can\'t do
UnsendVault doesn\'t connect to any chat service and can\'t recover anything from servers. It only sees what Android shows in notifications.

Keep capture running on devices that stop background apps

Android connects UnsendVault\'s notification listener on its own, and the app doesn\'t need to stay open. Some phones still stop or disconnect background services to save battery. These steps make capture more reliable.
In the list that opens, find UnsendVault and choose “Don\'t optimize” or “Unrestricted”.
Allow Autostart for UnsendVault, and set its battery saver to “No restrictions”.
In Device care → Battery, make sure UnsendVault isn\'t in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”, and add it to “Never sleeping apps”.
In App launch, set UnsendVault to “Manage manually” and allow auto-launch and running in background.
Allow Auto launch (or Startup manager) for UnsendVault and allow background activity in its battery settings.
Allow background startup for UnsendVault and allow high background power consumption.
Allow Auto launch for UnsendVault and set battery optimization to “Don\'t optimize”.
In Mobile Manager, allow Auto-start for UnsendVault.
Look for an auto-start or background activity setting for UnsendVault.
Turn UnsendVault off and on again in Notification access. This forces Android to reconnect the listener.
Tip: some phones let you lock an app in the Recents screen so it isn\'t cleared by “Close all”.

These settings differ between manufacturers and Android versions. If a button opens the wrong screen, use the app info page instead. Even with every step done, the system may still stop capture in rare cases.
What UnsendVault can and can\'t save, licenses
UnsendVault keeps an on-device archive of the message previews Android shows in notifications. It is an independent app and not affiliated with any messaging service.

resources.string: A message is marked possibly deleted only when the app itself showed a deletion notice for it, such as “This message was deleted”, and the stored notice is shown with it. A notification disappearing is never treated as a deletion; apps clear notifications for many ordinary reasons.

string-array.name: about_android_notes
string-array.item: Android 15 and later: one-time passwords and other sensitive notification content are hidden from notification listeners that the system doesn\'t trust. These messages appear as “Hidden by Android”.

Android 17: the system may withhold the text of messaging notifications from notification listeners that are not on its allowlist. Affected messages appear as “Hidden by Android” and their text can\'t be saved.
Some manufacturers stop background services aggressively; see Battery & reliability.
